text:
maria: quick follow-up from today's allocator sync — i'm sketching a 'nearline hotswap' handoff for evicting large KV-cache pages when GPU memory spikes. idea is a lightweight protocol between runtime allocator and paging controller so we can avoid full pause+swap cycles.

cheng: curious, how does that differ from current async-offload?

maria: current async-offload writes pages to host and signals completion. hotswap adds a 2-phase handoff: mark->freeze->handoff. freeze prevents concurrent writes to page metadata while we snapshot the minimal header then schedule DMA. goal: reduce pinned-region lifetime and avoid long mutex holds.

noah: +1 to reducing pinned time. worried about races with refcount and eviction callbacks though.

maria: agreed. plan is to add a small per-page 'handoff token' (uint32) and a fast-path check: if token==0 normal refcount path, else use handoff path that queues a lightweight continuation.

samir: can you paste the proto for the token state?

maria: sure:

```
struct HandoffToken {
  uint32_t seq; // monotonic per-page transition id
  uint8_t flags; // bit0 == HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS
}
```

maria: transition sequence: set token.flags bit, snapshot header, increment seq, drop heavy locks, enqueue DMA op pointing at seq. When DMA done, handler checks seq before freeing.

cheng: sounds promising. how do we ensure compatibility with existing slab allocator that expects immediate free?

noah: we can add a short quarantine window on free path: if HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS set, convert free into a deferred free callback. standard slab free becomes: if (token.flags) queue_deferred_free(ptr, token.seq); else free_immediate(ptr);

emily: what's the perf cost of the extra token check? we run tight loops in small-allocation fast paths.

maria: token read is a single atomic load (relaxed) on the hot path. For small allocations that never go near GPU residency it's a tiny cost. We should microbench but expect <1% in worst-case.

samir: failure modes? what if host OOM or DMA stalls?

maria: we add a fallback timer per-handoff. if DMA doesn't complete in X ms we clear HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS and fallback to conservative global pause (existing fallback). also record metrics (handoff_retries, fallback_count).

infra-bot: deploy-checker: note added - must add unit tests for deferred_free ordering and stress test for concurrent handoff.

maria: yes, tests: (1) single-page handoff race harness, (2) multi-page burst under high allocation churn, (3) simulated DMA timeouts assert no leaks.

cheng: one more: how does this interact with KV cache prefix reuse? if we snapshot header and later rebind a new mapping at same virtual addr we need seq mismatch to prevent double-free. seq solves that but we must guarantee wraparound is rare.

noah: use 32-bit seq plus checking on reuse should be fine; also increment by large delta on allocator recycle to reduce collision window.

emily: for on-prem customers with slower PCIe, we might need longer timers or adaptive backoff. suggest exposing config knobs per-deployment.

maria: agreed — will make timers adaptive based on historical DMA latency per-region. Also expose a safe default.

samir: ok next action items?

maria: (1) prototype token + freeze in runtime repo (branch: nearline-hotswap), (2) microbench perf on small-allocation path, (3) unit/stress tests, (4) add metrics and config knobs. i'll open RFC follow-up PR with design + pseudocode.

noah: assign me to the stress tests.

cheng: i'll review the PR and run perf.

emily: i'll wire up adaptive timer config in infra templates.

maria: thanks! tagging offline: @samir please keep an eye on safety checks for dedicated nodes.

samir: will do.

infra-bot: reminder: please add feature flag gating for initial rollout.

maria: yep — feature flag + canary on 2 nodes first.

noah: :thumbsup:

maria: wrapping up — i'll post the RFC-PR link here once ready.
